synopsis: AutoDRIVE is a digital-twin framework used in an off-road braking study; Samak et al. reported at GVSETS 2024 that its open-source framework supported vision-guided AEB across 128 simulated off-road test cases on high-performance computing clusters [f15934, f467]. In 2024, the AutoDRIVE team built an off-road greensward twin from a single lidar run, presented alongside forest MLS as an example of off-road lidar surveying [f3802, f4215]. The team claims a “sub-millimeter-level accurate” twin with a reported mean of 2.28e-4 m [f3860]. That accuracy figure requires caution because it appears to measure self-consistency against the team's own point cloud rather than independent ground truth [f3861].

relations.note: Specifies the braking study's scale, computing infrastructure, framework availability, and reporting venue.
Adds a concrete off-road twin construction example and its acquisition method.
The single lidar run substantiates greensward's inclusion as an off-road lidar surveying example.
Adds the team's claimed accuracy figure for the constructed twin.
Questions claimed accuracy because the apparent reference is self-consistency, not independent ground truth.
